title: He Called the 1987 Crash. Now He’s Calling This
creator: MarketBeat
summary: MarketBeat interviews Dr Mark Skousen of the Oxford Club (auto-captions garble his name as 'Scousson'), the economist credited with calling the 1987 crash, about whether this bull run survives and where to turn if it does not. His main threat is rising interest rates: a $2 trillion deficit at full employment forces heavy Treasury issuance just as AI data-centre borrowing competes for capital, while stubborn inflation — from the Middle East war's effect on oil and from tariffs — keeps rates up. He expects at most a bear market or correction rather than a 1987-style crash, citing circuit breakers and government intervention, and notes his Gross Output measure shows B2B supply-chain spending suddenly up almost 14% in real terms in the second quarter, which he reads as a business boom that could make any recession temporary. For positioning he prefers broad exposure: he recommends the XLK technology ETF over stock-picking, likes fee-based pipeline names such as Williams and Enterprise Products Partners for their rising dividends, sees the Global X Uranium ETF and Cameco as a contrarian group possibly bottoming after a year-long bear market (uranium $90 a pound), and calls Southern Copper and Freeport-McMoRan great, more conservative copper plays with copper near $7 a pound. He has moved from Kinross Gold, up almost 300% last year then down 50%, to Franco-Nevada for its revenue royalties and rising dividend. The calls are XLK, SCCO, FCX and FNV — BUY (guest recommendations); WMB, EPD, URA, CCJ and KGC — UNCERTAIN mentions.

calls.video_title: He Called the 1987 Crash. Now He’s Calling This
calls.thesis: BUY, first tracked XLK call for MarketBeat (guest Dr Mark Skousen, Oxford Club; no flip) — 'I recommend XLK, which is the technology fund': his preferred way to own new technology is a broad-based ETF or mutual fund because picking individual winners is luck. He says XLK has outperformed QQQ by about 30% (per year, as captioned) and has kept up with the S&P 500 this year.
calls.base_case: XLK holds Apple, Microsoft, Broadcom and Palantir (captions garble it as 'Palunteer') — mainly software and established tech; it does not hold Tesla or SpaceX, which he sees as high-risk, high-potential.
calls.bull_case: Broad diversification removes single-stock risk in a sector where winners are hard to pick in advance, while tech/AI remains, in his words, a golden age of investing technology and the main driver of the market.
calls.bear_case: Tech multiples are high and he is cautious overall: rising rates, stubborn inflation and high AI multiples mean investors 'have to be very careful' even in the one area still working.

calls.video_title: He Called the 1987 Crash. Now He’s Calling This
calls.thesis: BUY reiterated for MarketBeat (guest Dr Mark Skousen; was BUY in an earlier MarketBeat video, no flip) — Southern Copper is one of two copper names he calls 'great companies': 'if you want something a little more conservative, I think going into the copper stocks is the way to go.' No share price stated; copper itself is at an all-time high approaching $7 a pound (stated).
calls.base_case: Copper demand is being driven by data centres and by an ageing national infrastructure that has to be rebuilt, including chips and electrical build-out.
calls.bull_case: Supply is strained: very few new copper mines exist, so higher demand meets limited supply — he thinks copper prices can keep rising well beyond current levels.
calls.bear_case: A strong dollar (if interest rates keep rising) hurts the mining industry generally; metal prices are volatile and other guests have warned copper may not be near a top — or may be extended after a wild run.

calls.video_title: He Called the 1987 Crash. Now He’s Calling This
calls.thesis: BUY reiterated for MarketBeat (guest Dr Mark Skousen; was BUY in earlier MarketBeat videos, no flip) — Freeport-McMoRan (captions render it 'Freeport Macmaran') is the second copper name he calls a great company and part of 'the way to go' for a more conservative resources position. No share price stated.
calls.base_case: Same copper base case as Southern Copper: data-centre and infrastructure demand against very few new mines; copper approaching $7 a pound, an all-time high (stated).
calls.bull_case: Limited supply across copper, platinum, gold and silver with demand rising gives miners pricing power if commodity prices hold or spike.
calls.bear_case: Strong-dollar / higher-rate risk to miners; commodity cyclicality — he himself notes resource names can fall hard (his Kinross example fell 50% this year after a near-300% rise).

calls.video_title: He Called the 1987 Crash. Now He’s Calling This
calls.thesis: BUY, first tracked FNV call for MarketBeat (guest Dr Mark Skousen; no flip) — Franco-Nevada is the royalty company he likes and says he has moved on to: 'I like the royalty companies like Franco Nevada. FNV is one that I like,' and it is 'a better, safer way to go right now.' No share price stated.
calls.base_case: Royalties are based on a percentage of revenues rather than profit margins, and Franco-Nevada has a rising dividend policy — income that cushions falls in a cautious market.
calls.bull_case: A safer way to own gold/commodity upside while supply stays constrained: royalty names 'don't go up as fast, but they don't go down as fast either.'
calls.bear_case: By his own framing the trade-off is slower upside; the position still depends on gold and commodity prices, which a persistently strong dollar would pressure.
